name: com.boternity/boternity
title: BOTERNITY
description: Free MCP tools: read and watch web pages, audit MCP servers, data tools, agent notebooks, prompts.

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Read a public web page as clean text, with headings kept as Markdown, plus title, description, language, canonical URL, Open Graph, schema.org types, outline and optionally links. Use it when you need the content of a page now. robots.txt is respected and results are cached 10 minutes; long pages are paginated.

url.description: Public http(s) URL of the page.

start_index.description: Character offset to continue a long page (default 0).

include_links.description: Also return the links found on the page (default false).

tools.name: watch_page
tools.description: Start watching a public page: it is re-read on a schedule and each change is recorded as a diff with the sections that changed. Use it to follow prices, policies, docs or announcements over days. Optional: watch only one part of the page with a CSS selector, track keywords, and receive a webhook POST on change. Returns a watch id for get_watch. Watches end after 30 days.

url.description: Public http(s) URL of the page.

selector.description: CSS selector of the part to watch: tag, .class, #id, tag.class, or descendants such as 'main .price'.

keywords.description: Words to track; with a webhook, only keyword events are sent.

webhook_url.description: https URL that receives a JSON POST when the page changes.

tools.name: get_watch
tools.description: Get the state of a page watch created with watch_page: last check, HTTP status, number of changes, and the most recent diffs with changed sections and keyword events.

history.description: Number of recent changes to return (default 5).

tools.name: check_watch_now
tools.description: Schedule an immediate re-check of a page watch instead of waiting for its interval (at most once every 10 minutes per watch). Then read the result with get_watch.

tools.name: stop_watch
tools.description: Stop a page watch and delete the stored copy of the page. Use it when the watch is no longer needed.

tools.name: test_mcp_server
tools.description: Start an audit of a remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP) from the outside. It checks initialize, version negotiation, sessions, tools/list schemas and their token cost, ping, error codes, resources, prompts, CORS, Origin handling and latency, then scores the server out of 100 with fixes. Returns an id; read the report with get_mcp_test after about 30 seconds. Only audit servers you run or are allowed to test.

name.description: Tool name on the audited server.

tools.name: find_mcp_server
tools.description: Find the most reliable public remote MCP servers for a need, e.g. postgres, github, web search, send email, weather, payments. Uses the BOTERNITY MCP Index, which checks every server of the official MCP Registry each night: returns endpoint URL, score out of 100, grade, tool count, context tokens, latency, 30-day availability and a link to a comparison page. Use it before adding an MCP server to an agent.

need.description: What the server should do or connect to, e.g. postgres, github, web search, send email, weather.

min_score.description: Only servers scoring at least this (default 0).

include_auth.description: Also list servers that require sign-in (not scored) after the healthy ones (default false).

tools.name: get_mcp_test
tools.description: Get the report of an audit started with test_mcp_server: status (queued, running, done), score, grade, each check with how-to-fix advice, latency and a Markdown version to share.

tools.name: create_notebook
tools.description: Create a private persistent notebook and get its secret token. Use it as long-term memory across sessions: notes are kept for 30 days after the last use. Store the token yourself; it cannot be recovered.

tools.name: write_note
tools.description: Save a note in your notebook, or replace the note that already has this name. Text up to 8000 characters.

notebook.description: Secret notebook token returned by create_notebook.

key.description: Note name, e.g. todo or project/status.

value.description: Note text: plain text, Markdown or JSON.

tools.name: read_notes
tools.description: Read one note by name, or list the notes of your notebook (names, sizes, update times) when no name is given, optionally filtered by a name prefix.

notebook.description: Secret notebook token returned by create_notebook.

key.description: Name of the note to read; omit to list notes.

prefix.description: When listing, only names starting with this prefix.

tools.name: delete_note
tools.description: Delete one note from your notebook.

notebook.description: Secret notebook token returned by create_notebook.

key.description: Note name, e.g. todo or project/status.

tools.name: convert_data
tools.description: Convert data between JSON, CSV and XML: json→csv (array of flat objects), csv→json (header line required), xml→json (attributes as @name, text as #text) and json→xml. Reports the position of syntax errors.

data.description: The data as text: the JSON, CSV or XML document to convert.

tools.name: inspect_json
tools.description: Check whether a text is valid JSON (exact line and column of an error), or extract a value with a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) such as /items/0/name; when the path breaks, says where and which keys exist.

pointer.description: Optional RFC 6901 pointer; omit to only validate.

tools.name: analyze_table
tools.description: Per-column statistics of a table: count, missing, distinct and type; min, max, sum, mean, median and standard deviation for numbers (numeric strings such as 1,5 included); most frequent values for text.

rows.description: Table as an array of flat JSON objects (one per row), up to 500 rows.

tools.name: compare_tables
tools.description: Compare two versions of a table: with a key column, rows added, removed and changed cell by cell; without a key, rows added and removed.

before.description: Table as an array of flat JSON objects (one per row), up to 500 rows.

after.description: Table as an array of flat JSON objects (one per row), up to 500 rows.

key.description: Column that identifies a row, e.g. id (optional).

tools.name: clean_table
tools.description: Clean a table: trim spaces, turn empty strings into null, remove duplicate rows, and optionally parse numeric strings (1,5 or 1 234) and normalize column names to snake_case. Returns the cleaned rows and a report.

rows.description: Table as an array of flat JSON objects (one per row), up to 500 rows.

parse_numbers.description: Convert numeric strings to numbers (default false).

tools.name: compare_texts
tools.description: Line-by-line unified diff between two texts, with counts of added and removed lines and a similarity ratio.

tools.name: get_current_time
tools.description: Current date and time in UTC or any IANA timezone, with weekday, UTC offset and Unix time. Use it whenever you need to know the present moment.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name, e.g. Europe/Paris or America/New_York. Default UTC.

tools.name: convert_time
tools.description: Convert an ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 date-time to another IANA timezone, handling daylight saving time.

datetime.description: Date-time, e.g. 2026-03-29T01:30:00Z, or without offset with from_timezone.

from_timezone.description: IANA timezone of a date-time without offset.

to_timezone.description: IANA timezone name, e.g. Europe/Paris or America/New_York. Default UTC.

tools.name: compute_duration
tools.description: Exact duration between two ISO 8601 date-times, in seconds, minutes, hours and days, with a breakdown.

tools.name: list_cron_runs
tools.description: Next run times of a 5-field cron expression (minute hour day month weekday) in any IANA timezone.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name, e.g. Europe/Paris or America/New_York. Default UTC.

after.description: Start from this ISO 8601 date-time (default now).

tools.name: encode_text
tools.description: Base64, base64url and URL encoding or decoding of text, or a hash (SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-1, MD5) in hex and base64.

tools.name: generate_uuid
tools.description: Generate random version 4 UUIDs, for identifiers in test data, records or requests.

tools.name: parse_url
tools.description: Split a URL into scheme, host, port, path, decoded query parameters and fragment.

tools.name: explain_http_status
tools.description: Official reason phrase of an HTTP status code, the specification that defines it, and whether a client should retry.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the verified resources of the BOTERNITY catalog by keywords (all words must match the title or source), or list them all: exact extracts of specifications (MCP, HTTP, OpenAPI, robots.txt) with their source.

query.description: Keywords, e.g. 'mcp session' or 'retry-after'. Omit to list everything.

tools.name: read_catalog_resource
tools.description: Read one verified catalog resource by id: the extracts and the URL of their source.

tools.name: request_resource
tools.description: Tell BOTERNITY which knowledge or tool you are missing. The request is reviewed privately and may lead to a new catalog resource or tool. Returns an id for get_request_status. Do not include personal data.

need.description: What you need, in one or two sentences.

tools.name: get_request_status
tools.description: Get the status of a request made with request_resource: received, or resource available with its link.
